sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:1
items.html:
A record in the place where Yesod had been: It has already been explained that the Malchut of Akudim is called Tabur, and her Emanator, which is the secret of the Malchut of the Rosh [head], is called Peh [mouth]. And when the screen in the Malchut of the Guf [body] was refined of all the coarseness included in it, and remained refined in complete equality with the Malchut of the Rosh, which is its Emanator, as is known, this is called Malchut having returned and ascended to the Emanator; for when both of them are equal in the measure of refinement, they are then found to be attached to and included in one another as one phase. For it is known that disparity of form is the measure of difference and separation in spiritual things, and equivalence of form is the attachment and the union in spiritual things. Therefore, at the time when the Malchut of the Guf and the Malchut of the Rosh are found equal in the measure of refinement, they are then discerned as attached one to the other and included in one phase, as written in the previous parts.
And this is what he says: “And that record never departs from there, even when Malchut returns and ascends to the Emanator.” And he informs us by this that even at the time when the screen has been refined of all its coarseness entirely, until it remained equal to the refinement of the Emanator, nevertheless the screen is still included of the records of the ten Sefirot of the Guf — except for the record of phase four, for the last phase does not leave a record, for the reason explained above: that these records are of direct light, and the last phase does not receive direct light into herself, and there is in her only reflected light alone, as is known.
And know that the matter of these records, which remained included in Malchut even at the time of her being included in the Emanator, is the entire seed for the birth of the second Partzuf, for from these records all the lights and the vessels are drawn to the second Partzuf, as written above (and in the Inner Observation here, Item 52). This is because the screen of the Malchut of the Rosh is never refined, and the coupling by striking in the screen of phase four that is there is in the phase of an unceasing coupling. Hence it is found that when the Malchut of the Guf ascends there and is included in the screen of the Rosh, she too is included in the coupling of the Rosh, and this causes the awakening of the coarseness included in the records that are in her, for she receives from the phase of the coarseness from below upward that is included there in the screen of the Rosh. Indeed, as soon as the records in her return to their coarseness, it is found that it is turned in them into a coarseness from above downward, since they come from the ten Sefirot of the Guf, where they had already been in the phase of clothing from above downward. And out of this there returned and was revealed there the phase of the Guf in the screen that ascended, which is a coarseness from above downward, which is Guf and not Rosh; and this revelation is discerned as a phase of descent and separation from the Malchut of the Rosh, for it returned to its former state, to the Malchut of the phase of the Guf — yet not to phase four, which is called Tabur, but only to phase three, which is called the chest. And there the coupling by striking is made anew, which brings forth ten Sefirot in the level of Hochma in Rosh, Toch and Sof [end]. And it is called the Partzuf AB. And this matter has already been explained (in Part 3, answer 210). And from there seek it.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:2
items.html: The record is from the first light: From the first expansion, which expands from the Peh [mouth] until the Tabur of AK. And behold it is composed of direct light and reflected light clothed one in the other, for direct light is called refined light and reflected light is called coarse light (as written in the Inner Light, Chapter 2, Item 10). The remainder that is left over from the refined light after its departure is called by the name “record,” and it is mercy, since it is a remnant of the direct light that is drawn from above downward, to the phase of clothing in the Partzuf. And the reflected light that was emptied of the direct light after its departure is discerned as the phase of the vessels within which were clothed the records that remained from the direct light — as in the words of the ARI above, Item 10.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:3
items.html: And light that comes by way of returning upward is reflected light: Meaning, a light that comes and is drawn from the Emanator by reason of the coupling by striking that is made upon the screen within the degrees of its refinement; for then the levels grow progressively smaller until the light disappears entirely and returns to its root above, to the Malchut of the Rosh [head]. And these levels are called reflected light and judgment, by reason of their appearing at the time of the departure.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:4
items.html: Their faces were downward: There is here no movement whatsoever, and no nape and no weariness. Rather, as was explained in the previous parts, that any renewal of form whatsoever is called by the name spiritual movement (see Inner Observation, Part 1, Item 33). And know that the phase of bestowal in the terms of the lights, or the phase of drawing in the terms of the vessels, is called by the name “face.” And it is known that everyone who bestows bestows into the coarser thing, and the coarser the screen is, the higher the level of ten Sefirot that is bestowed there. Therefore the lights of mercy, which are bestowed in the phase of clothing in the Partzuf, are discerned here as having their faces downward; for the word “face” means bestowal, and “downward” means the greater coarseness. “And their faces were downward” means that the bestowal takes hold in the phase of the greater coarseness that is in the degree.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:5
items.html: They turned their faces upward toward the Emanator: It has already been explained that the phase of bestowal is called face, and from it it is understood that the phase of departure from bestowal is called posterior. It was also explained that “downward” means the coarser phase that is there. “And their posterior downward” means that the lights depart and withdraw themselves from the coarseness, in such a way that in the phase where the coarseness is greater, there the departure will be greater.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:6
items.html: The light of the Emanator is never cut off: This is a great principle in the wisdom: that the upper light goes on and flows always, without cessation or change whatsoever, in the secret of the verse “I, HaVaYaH, have not changed,” etc., as we expanded upon this in Part 1 (in the Inner Light, Chapter 2, Item 2). Therefore, even at the time of departure — that is, at the time when the screen goes on and is refined — although this departure was all at once and in a single instant, nevertheless, since the refinement necessarily rises in the order of the degrees that are in the four phases of coarseness, for it necessarily is refined first to phase three, and afterwards to phase two, and afterwards to phase one, and afterwards to the phase of Keter — therefore it is discerned by us that the light of the Emanator, which does not cease, expands to it and couples with it at the time of its ascent and its coming from phase to phase; and in each phase it brings forth a new level of ten Sefirot according to the measure of the coarseness in it: for upon its coming to phase three it brings forth the level of Hochma, and upon its coming to phase two it brings forth the level of Bina, etc., until it is refined entirely, and the upper light ceases for lack of reflected light to clothe it, for there is no revelation of light without a vessel and a garment.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:7
items.html:
From the Emanator to the lower ones through them and by their mediation: Meaning that a light descends from the Emanator to the lower phases that were made in each and every Sefira by way of the ascent of the screen and its refinement; for in every place to which the screen in Malchut ascended, that place became a lower phase — the meaning of which is that she cuts off the light of the Emanator and restrains it from expanding from her downward, so that the light of the Emanator is found to terminate in that place; and therefore we call the place to which the screen comes by the name lower phase.
And this is what the ARI is precise about: “to the lower ones through them and by their mediation,” to inform us that the light is drawn from the Emanator only through the lower phases and by the mediation of the lower phases, that is, by means of the screen that raises reflected light, in the course of its ascent and its coming in the degrees of its refinement. For upon its coming to phase three, which is ZA, behold phase three becomes a lower phase which strikes the upper light and restrains it from expanding from it downward. And it is found that the whole measure of the light that was fit to be received in it is repelled back to its posterior in the secret of reflected light, and it draws ten Sefirot in the level of Hochma, as above, etc., in this way. And you find that the drawing of the light always comes from a lower phase that has been renewed, in that the light which she did not receive became reflected light, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:8
items.html: Keter returned and ascended to the Emanator: That is, by reason of the refinement of the screen from phase four to phase three, the reflected light that rises from phase three does not reach to clothe the light of Keter, and therefore it returned and ascended to its root, for there is no revelation of light without a garment, as is known. And this departure of the light of Keter is called by the name “the posterior of Keter”; for face means bestowal and expansion, and posterior means departure from bestowal.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:9
items.html: Receives only from the posterior of Keter alone: Posterior means departure, as above. And behold, in the first expansion all the Sefirot emerged in the level of Keter, and it is found that all the Sefirot received from the phase of the face of Keter, since they were equal with it in level. This is not so at the time of refinement; for at the time when it was refined to phase three and the level of Hochma emerged, and the light of Keter remained concealed in the Peh [mouth], it is now found that Hochma receives from the posterior of Keter — meaning that she suffers and feels the great lack from the concealment of the light of Keter. And this is what he says, “that Hochma receives from the posterior of Keter,” that is, the phase of judgment from the lack of its illumination which she feels, as stated; and in this way with the rest of the Sefirot.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:10
items.html: Malchut receives from nine phases of posterior: For this is the rule, that all the forces that are in the upper are always found in the one below it, which necessarily receives all the posterior that is in its upper. So at the time when it was refined to phase three and the level of Hochma emerged, and she received the phase of judgment that is revealed in her from the lack of the illumination of the light of Keter, as above, then also the Sefirot below Hochma likewise receive that same posterior; for they too received from the face of Keter in the first expansion, just as Hochma did, since all of them were there in an equal level up to Keter, and now, in the level of phase three, they are found lacking the light of Keter, and they have nothing but the light of the face of Hochma. And in this way, when it was refined from phase three to phase two and the level of Bina emerged, so that Bina is now found suffering also from the departure of the light of Hochma, and is found receiving into herself two phases of posterior, which are: the posterior of Keter, which she already received at the time of her being in the level of phase three, and the posterior of Hochma, which she receives now — behold, the Sefirot below Bina likewise suffer from that same posterior of Hochma, in addition to the posterior of Keter which they received at the time of the appearance of the level of phase three. And so on in this way, until the time when it was refined to the phase of Keter, where only the level of Malchut alone emerged, and all the first nine were lacking there; and Malchut is found receiving from nine posteriors. For at the time of her being in the level of phase three she received the posterior of Keter; and at the time of her being in phase two she received the posterior of Hochma; and at the time of her being in phase one she received the posterior of Bina; and now, when she has nothing but her own light alone, she receives also from the posterior of ZA, which are the six Sefirot HGT NHY. Thus Malchut received nine phases of posterior.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:11
items.html: From the Peh [mouth] outward and downward until the Tabur: That is, the first expansion, in which the coupling by striking emerged upon phase four, which is called Peh, which is the phase of the Malchut of the Rosh [head]; after which this Malchut widened out into ten Sefirot of herself and within herself, down to her own Malchut. And these ten Sefirot are called Guf [body], and the Malchut of the Guf is called Tabur (as above). And the ten Sefirot of this Rosh and Guf were in the level of Keter (as above).

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:12
items.html: The record that the first light left over: See in the words of the ARI above (Chapter 2, Item 10), where he wrote that two lights remained after the departure of the first expansion, which are: the first is the light that remained from direct light; and the second is the coarse light, the meaning of which is reflected light that was emptied of the direct light which it had clothed at the time of the first expansion, and remained below, and the coarseness in it was revealed. And this coarse light is the secret of the vessels. And the refined light that remained from the direct light is called a record, and this record remained clothed within the coarse light. (See there, and in the Inner Light, ibid.)

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:13
items.html: At the time when the lights were ascending and returning from below upward: “Ascending” means refinement from the coarseness, in order to come into equivalence of form with its upper, that is, the Emanator. “Returning” means the departure of the light after its expansion, which is discerned as its returning to its root. And this is what he says: “the light drawn from the Emanator to the Sefira, and it is drawn at the time when the lights were ascending and returning.” The meaning is, the upper light that is drawn by means of the coupling by striking at the time of the refinement of the screen and its coming into the degrees in the course of its refinement; for then the levels grow progressively smaller, until it is refined entirely and equalises its form with the Emanator, that is, with the Malchut of the Rosh [head] (as above). And this matter is always called “the ascent of the lights to the Emanator.” And remember this.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:14
items.html:
And descends downward to shine in the Sefira: The degrees are discerned one toward the other in the phase of a father toward sons (as above in the words of the ARI, Chapter 2, Item 3). Therefore, at the time of the ascent of the lights to the Emanator, at the time when the screen was refined from phase four to phase three, so that the coupling was then made in phase three, and phase four remained empty of her light — behold, then phase three bestows upon phase four from the illumination of its coupling. And likewise after this, when phase three is refined to phase two, so that the coupling is in phase two, and then phase three too remains empty of light — behold, then phase two bestows upon phase three from the illumination of its coupling; etc., in this way. And although from the side of the drawing of the lights phase four is reckoned as Keter and phase three as Hochma, indeed in the terms of the vessels in themselves it is the opposite, that phase three is reckoned as ZA and phase four as Malchut. And since phase four is empty of light, therefore there is nothing to discern here except in the terms of the vessels according to themselves. And so all of them, in this way.
And this is what he says: “when the third light, called reflected light, is drawn and descends downward to shine in the Sefira.” The third light means the light of the levels that emerge in the course of its refinement, as above. And behold, that light is drawn and descends also below the place of the coupling, to shine to the Sefira which is beneath it (that is, as above); for at the time when the coupling is in phase two, the illumination of the coupling is drawn to the Sefira below it, which is phase three, empty of light. And it is known that the lights left records in the Sefirot after their departure from there; and therefore, at the time when the illumination of the coupling of phase two is drawn to phase three, it meets there the light of her record.
And this is what he says: “it then meets the second light, called the record, which remained below.” That is, as explained, that the light of the coupling that is in the upper phase is drawn and descends to the lower phase, which is empty of her light, and it meets the record there. And further on the ARI calls that light which descends from the illumination of the coupling downward by the name “the descending reflected light.”

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:15
items.html:
Divided in their nature: The meaning is that the record is of direct light, remaining from the first expansion, whose level is up to Keter, since the coupling by striking was made there in the screen of phase four. And behold, because of this the coarseness of phase four is reckoned for it as its phase of face, for from her is drawn to it the whole height of its level; while coarseness from phase three and upward is reckoned for it as the posterior of its vessel, and it does not shine for it.
And its opposite is the reflected light that descends to it from the illumination of the coupling of the upper phase. For example, when the illumination of the coupling of phase two descends to the Sefira of phase three, which was emptied of her light, as above — behold, that descending reflected light comes from a coupling by striking that was made in the screen of the coarseness of phase two, whose level is up to Bina; and the coarseness of phase two is reckoned for it as its phase of face, that is, as the utmost height of its level, and it leaves the coarseness of phase three and phase four as a phase of posterior, that is, as lowliness and deficiency. For since they do not shine for it, it is found that it lowers them and casts them downward — meaning that the disparity of form in them becomes a separator upon the light. That is, the opposite of the record, in which the coarser phase four draws and joins with the greater light, as above.
And this is what he says: “And behold they are divided in their nature, for the one is direct light and mercy, and the other is reflected light and judgment.” For the records that remain in all the Sefirot come from direct light and mercy, that is, from the first expansion, in which the coupling emerged upon the screen of phase four, where the coarser a thing is the more esteemed it is, since it is entirely mercy. But the reflected light that descends from the illumination of the couplings which emerge at the time of the refinement — behold, all these levels are reckoned as reflected light and judgment, since they depart from the coarseness and lower and cast the coarseness down to a phase of posterior, as above. Therefore the light that descends from them is in contradiction to the records, in which the coarser is the more important, as explained. And it is found that what is reckoned as a phase of face with respect to the record is reckoned as a phase of posterior with respect to the descending reflected light; and what is reckoned as a phase of face with respect to the descending reflected light is reckoned as a phase of posterior with respect to the record. And therefore they strike and clash one against the other.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:16
items.html: The record longs and desires to ascend to its source: For since she is the portion remaining of the first expansion, which has already departed and become concealed in its source, this longing and this desire are found imprinted in the record as well. And this is what he says: “and although it is not actual, for the record remains in existence below forever, nevertheless its longing and its desire are to ascend.” Meaning, although the record is designated to remain in the vessel, and she will never ascend to her source, nevertheless there is in her the desire to ascend, since the force of the whole of the light necessarily remains imprinted in her.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:17
items.html:
But the reflected light descends downward: The meaning is that it comes and is drawn from the Emanator by a renewed coupling, and descends downward for clothing within the Guf [body]; for all these couplings that emerge in the degrees of its refinement are made in the Rosh [head], and from there they are drawn from above downward to the Guf. Only, for the reason that they emerge at the time of refinement and it is not destined to endure, it is discerned as reflected light and judgment, as above.
And this is what he says: “But the reflected light descends downward.” Meaning, if one reckons only with the time of the coupling, it is found to expand and to descend for its hour, for clothing in the Guf; which is not so with the record, in which there is the desire to depart from the Guf and to ascend to her source, as above.
And know that for this reason the reflected light that descends from the illumination of the coupling is found to overpower the light of the record at the time of their striking and their clashing one against the other. Therefore sparks were separated from this reflected light and clothe themselves within the vessel that is empty of light; and the light of the record is found repelled from her interior, and it ascended above that vessel, in the secret of Tagin [crownlets] upon the letters. As the ARI wrote (further on, Chapter 4, Item 4), that the two of them cannot be in one vessel, since they are opposite to one another (as above). And know that the striking and clashing spoken of is made above the empty vessel; for the record strikes the reflected light and does not permit it to expand, and the descending reflected light strikes the record in order to clothe itself and shine in the vessel — until sparks were separated from the reflected light, and they descend and come within the vessel.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:18
items.html: The vessels: In which the light afterwards returned and expanded, a second expansion, in the level of Hochma, where Keter remained concealed in the Peh [mouth], and the light of Hochma clothed itself in the vessel of Keter, and the light of Bina in the vessel of Hochma, etc., until Malchut remained without light, as written further on. And know that these sparks were prepared as vessels for these lights, as written above in the Inner Light, Chapter 2, Item 3.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:19
items.html:
There were in them phases of vessels: So the ARI wrote explicitly above, Chapter 2, Item 10: that the coarse light which remained after the departure of the light of the first expansion is the phases of the vessels themselves of the Partzuf, into which came the two lights mentioned, called: the second light, the record, and the fourth light, the falling sparks, called letters.
And this is what he says: “that already from the beginning there were in them phases of vessels, save that these sparks mingled and joined with them.” The meaning is that two phases of vessels must be prepared for the second expansion, for there is there in each Sefira a male and a Nukva, as the ARI wrote in Etz Chaim (Gate 7, Chapter 3). Therefore, from those phases of vessels which were in them from the beginning — that is, from the coarse light mentioned — from them were made the vessels for the lights of the males of the second expansion; and from the sparks that fell into them and mingled with them were made the vessels for the lights of the females of this expansion. And his saying “and mingled” is to inform us that the phases are not equal one to another, for the sparks of phase three came into phase four, and likewise the sparks of phase two into the vessel of phase three, and the sparks of phase one into the vessel of phase two, etc. And therefore this joining is discerned as a mingling. And understand this.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:3:20
items.html:
After the manner of the phase of the 288 sparks: A great thing he informs us here. For it is known that the phase of the 288 sparks which remained in the vessels after they broke and died were what caused the vessels to be revived, since these sparks were in the secret of the association of mercy with judgment, as written in their place. Just so the sparks here, which fell from the descending reflected light: they too are from the secret of the association of the attribute of mercy with judgment, only in the secret of the beginning. For every upper phase is reckoned as the attribute of mercy with respect to the phase below it; and since the sparks of the upper phase fell and mingled and joined with the lower phase, as above (see above item), this is reckoned as a mingling of the attribute of mercy with judgment, equally with the 288 sparks mentioned.
And know that this is the whole merit of the departure of the first expansion: for by reason of her the aforementioned sparks descended, and the root was made for the association of the attribute of mercy with judgment. And this is what the ARI notes further on concerning this departure, that it is the phase of a marring in order to correct; and this is similar to the breaking of the vessels, which likewise was in order to revive. And that is the association of the attribute of mercy with judgment, from which comes the reviving and from which comes all the correction of the world. And understand this. And it will be further explained in its place.
